Since `_control_bar` reads `app0` (the CURRENT active tab at render time, resolved independently of the POST's `app` form field) and does a one-shot pop-and-clear of `last_msg`, a real regression (e.g. active-tab/app0 mismatch, escaping bug, tone-mapping bug, message cleared before render) would not be caught by these tests even though the ticket's own AC explicitly calls for asserting on the rendered response. (Keeping euInflightBtn head-injected is fine since it's just a definition — only the DOM-scanning bootstrap must be deferred.)

Add a regression assertion in tests/eu741_inflight_button_test.py that catches the ordering defect: assert the helper's bootstrap is DOMContentLoaded/readyState-guarded (so a head-injected bootstrap that scans the DOM eagerly fails the test). String-presence checks alone cannot verify the feature actually binds.

issues.detail: _INFLIGHT_BUTTON_HELPER's bootstrap IIFE (cockpit_views.py:329-334) calls document.querySelectorAll('button[data-eu-inflight-btn]') synchronously, but _wrap injects the helper BEFORE {inner} (cockpit_views.py:368-369), i.e. in the head ahead of all body content. At execution time no button has been parsed yet, so the NodeList is empty and euInflightBtn is bound to nothing. The whole feature is inert in a real browser. The EU-717 sibling helper explicitly emits its bootstrap AFTER its controls for exactly this reason (cockpit_views.py:878-880); this ticket inverts that. tests/eu741_inflight_button_test.py only asserts substring presence in rendered HTML; it never models script/DOM execution order, so it cannot detect the head-before-body ordering bug and gives a false-green. Add an assertion that the bootstrap is DOMContentLoaded-guarded (grep the helper for a readiness gate) or that the button markup precedes the invoking script, so this class of ordering regression is caught in-repo.

Disabling the submit button inside the form's own 'submit' handler (lock() sets btn.disabled=true) is generally safe in modern browsers because submission is already in progress, but it is a known footgun in some engines. Since the three buttons carry no name/value needed by the POST it does not drop form data here — acceptable, but worth a comment noting the buttons must stay value-less.

All green. Summary of the picture and fix:

**Root cause of the iteration-1 rejection:** The EU-743 feature code itself was fully and correctly implemented in iteration 1 (composer double-Enter dedupe, `council.set_typing/is_typing` claim-clear flag with a `finally` that clears on both success and error, `/api/chat-thread` + poller rendering the `.typing` indicator). The stub lacked `set_typing`, so `_answer()` raised `AttributeError` before reaching `respond_to_commander`, and the "routes to the CTO chat" assertion went red (7/8). • /api/chat-thread + poller reconcile the .typing node, reusing the existing CSS at cockpit_views.py:1548.

• Only advisory minors (global-flag concurrency flicker, loose dict annotation); all ACs met — PASS.

issues.detail: council._typing_state is a single global bool with no reference count; two concurrent CTO replies would let the first thread's finally-clear turn off the indicator while a second reply is still generating (cosmetic flicker). Acceptable for the single-Commander cockpit, but a counter would be more robust.
_typing_state annotated as bare `dict` rather than `dict[str, bool]`; not Any, so it does not erode the type surface, just slightly loose.

## Summary

### What was done

**orchestrator/warroom.py** — Unified liveness scoring across three public helpers:
- **`live_runs()`**: Added optional `run_state` param. Scoring now uses `max(audit_ts, hb_ts)` instead of audit-only, so a model call >150s (zero audit events but fresh `last_activity` bumps) keeps tickets live. Heartbeat is inherited when ticket tid is in `run_tickets` (drain/concurrent builds) or falls back to app-matching for single-run contexts. Terminal-outcome filter and dedup preserved intact.
- **`active_run()`**: Forwards `run_state` to `live_runs()`. When both signals stale → idle fallback renders `outcome='running'` as `'interrupted'` chip (preserved).
- **`_run_in_flight()`**: Checks audit recency first (fast path), then falls back to `run_state['last_activity']` within the window. No callers break — old signatures unchanged.

**orchestrator/cockpit_

• All 5 ACs met: unified max(audit,heartbeat) liveness, live stage lit via EU-448, INTERRUPTED reserved for both-stale, run_started reset per ticket_start/pass, 5-check harness.
• No admitted-red tests; typing/error-handling clean.
• Minor: single-run fallback (warroom.py:1007) inherits the heartbeat to every outcomeless row when run_tickets is empty — could resurrect a ghost as false-live under cap>1 + cockpit drain; scope it to ts[0]'s ticket. Bounded by default cap=1.

issues.detail: warroom.py:1007 single-run heartbeat fallback `elif hb_ts and (t.get('app')==app or not app)` grants the heartbeat to EVERY outcomeless row of the app when run_tickets is empty, not just the running ticket. AC1 scopes the heartbeat to 'when the run-state's ticket matches'. Under max_concurrent_builders>1 + a cockpit /api/run drain (run_tickets=[], server.py:2032), a stale outcomeless ghost row (the docstring's own EU-474 example) could be resurrected as a false-live card — the inverse of the bug this ticket fixes. Bounded today by default cap=1 and by the concurrent path populating run_tickets via autopilot. Recommend scoping the fallback to ts[0]'s ticket_id.

_run_in_flight's EU-574 heartbeat fallback (warroom.py:1080) is dead in production: its sole caller (render_board:2069) never passes run_state, and it only runs when the cockpit did NOT start the run (this process's last_activity is then stale/None). Either wire run_state through or drop the branch.
